ShortDescription.Value: A better vanilla building menu: sorting, categories, filters and more details.

Publish.LongDescription:
A better version of the vanilla building menu, with sorting, categories and more details. Click any toolbar menu (Roads, Electricity, Education, Zones and the rest) and you get a panel instead of the row of icons.
* Grid, list, cards or table. Category tabs and a search box. * Sort by cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot, level or parking. * Group by type, theme, source, density, footprint, cost or progression. * Filter by unlocked, DLC, theme, asset pack, placement, role or source. Density has its own tabs. * Set a range for cost, upkeep, workers, capacity, lot width or lot depth. * Hover an asset to see its numbers and what unlocks it. * Building upgrades get names, cost and footprint too.
The list holds what the menu holds. Trees are under Landscaping; props, decals and hidden assets are not, and there is no object picker. Use Find It for those.
Works with Find It and does not replace it. Find It is a window over every asset in the game; this mod changes the toolbar menus. When Find It's window is open it takes the menu slot; this panel returns when it closes.
No Harmony patches, nothing saved to your city. Remove it any time.
**Options** (Options > Better Building Menu): switch back to the stock icon row; tile size; widen searches to every menu automatically.
Bugs and requests: the comments on this page.
Forked from Find It 1.5.8 by T. D. W. Thanks also to YenYang (UI), Algernon, Chameleon (icons) and Baka-gourd (focus handling).
This mod was developed with AI assistance (Anthropic's Claude), under human direction and review.
Publish.ChangeLog:
0.2.0
Changes * Each menu's tabs follow the game's own tab row, the menu picker follows the toolbar, and the All tab's headings follow the tabs. * Development tree tabs and headings use the game's own names, in the game's language, instead of English. * Education's school tabs and school-tier headings name each level after the game's own school, in the game's language. * Subcategory headings and labels, the All tab and chip, and theme names use the game's own words, in the game's language. In English, Paths reads Pathways, Shrubs & Bushes reads Bushes, and Extractor Zones reads Specialized Industry. * The Role filter and role headings use the game's name for each role, in the game's language. * An asset that several development tree nodes unlock is filed under one of them by a rule modelled on how the game unlocks it, instead of whichever came first. * Changing or clearing a filter or a range starts the list again at its first 100 rows. * The footer's counts group their digits the way the game does. * Replace the vanilla build menu takes effect at once, without a restart. Turning it off hands an open menu back to the game.
Asset details * Hovering an asset shows more of the game's own tooltip: pollution levels, a power plant's voltage, power line capacity on roads, transformer capacity, input and output, water pipes on roads, and transport stops. A network's cost includes its auxiliary networks. Most lines use the game's wording, in every language it ships. * An incinerator's Capacity is its garbage store, and its electricity gets a Power output line. * Power output adds up every source a building has instead of showing only the largest. * Zoned and signature buildings show no upkeep figure, as in the game's tooltip. The table's Upkeep column, sort and range skip them. * Upgrades read as the game reads them: Resource consumption -20 %, pollution changes as signed percentages, and graduation as +5 %. * Negative wellbeing, health and work conditions are shown with their sign. * Cemetery and crematorium capacity is a plain number, as in the game's tooltip. * Comfort is shown for parking and transport stops, a geothermal plant says it needs ground water, and a hydroelectric dam shows its own cost and upkeep. * Effects use the game's units, a shelter's vehicles read Evacuation buses, homes per cell keep a decimal, a road with no upkeep has no upkeep line, and deathcare processing rounds up.
Fixes * With a menu open, clicking a building on the map shows its info panel. * After a search, Enter picks the best match you can place, in every view. * A trailing space in the search box no longer loses matches. * With a tab selected, the number of matches elsewhere is what Search everything finds. * Typing in a filter's own search box no longer breaks the panel. * The resize edge stays under the cursor while dragging, at every resolution. * Load more says how many rows it adds, and a double click loads once. * The metric filter's badge counts the ranges set. * The category chip's picker offers only the tabs shown. * The Small Roads tab and heading no longer carry a stray line break. * The Content filter's icon is drawn. * The reverse-sort button's tooltip reads Reverse sort. * The Options screen shows its labels in English in the 13 languages that had none translated. * On a Turkish system, words such as Industrial are capitalised correctly. * If the panel fails while drawing, the game's own menu, upgrades picker or tool options take its place. If indexing fails, the panel keeps the city's last complete index. * With the upgrades picker open, the mouse wheel zooms and extensions can be placed above it. * A filter row with two icons keeps them on one line at every resolution. * Search everything shows its whole label at 1280x720. * Very long names are shortened in the middle in the list and card views.
Compatibility * Road Builder: an edited road is replaced in its menu and tab at once, numbered duplicates keep their numbers, and discarded roads no longer appear on a session's first load. * Find It: an asset whose tag names a category pair the panel does not have is listed under its own category instead of being dropped. * Asset UI Manager and other mods that move a category or an asset between menus: it gets one heading in the All tab, in its place.
Performance * Typing a search or dragging the resize edge no longer redraws every row. * The mod no longer copies every object and road in the city once a minute. * A full index pass no longer checks each building's mesh against every other's, and building or bulldozing a unique building no longer refreshes a closed panel.
